newsitem.title: USA: Senator agrees to clear Pena's nomination for vote.
newsitem.headline: Senator agrees to clear Pena's nomination for vote.

text.p: Senate Energy Committee Chairman Frank Murkowski said Tuesday he agreed to let his committee vote on the nomination of Federico Pena as U.S. energy secretary, lifting his block on the nomination.
The Alaska Republican said the committee would vote on Pena Thursday morning, and the nomination should move fairly quickly to the full Senate floor.

Murkowski, at a news conference, said he agreed to clear the vote after getting a letter from the White House which he said indicated the administration would be willing to work with him on the issue of storing radioactive waste accumulating at U.S. nuclear power plants.
Because of this, Murkowski said, he would move on his bill to set up an interim nuclear waste dump to start accepting spent fuel that the federal government legally takes title to next year.

"The administration has indicated it is committed to resolving the complex issue of nuclear storage," Murkowski said. The Senate last year passed Murkowski's bill to set up an interim dump in Nevada, but the House did not act on a similar bill after Clinton's veto threat.

The letter from White House Chief of Staff Erskine Bowles said the administration "is committed to resolving the complex and important issue of nuclear waste storage in a timely and sensible manner," but reaffirmed that Clinton would veto a bill that designated a temporary storage site before a study was completed on using Yucca Mountain in Nevada as a permanent site.
